stage_2_story.text_en:
Avi has always liked taking care of his own car. He says it saves money and teaches you something useful. Every few months, he spends a Sunday morning in the driveway doing basic maintenance.

This Sunday, the first thing he checked was the oil. He pulled out the dipstick and saw the oil was dark and old. He grabbed his wrench, removed the drain plug, and let the old oil run out into a metal pan. Then he poured in fresh oil and checked the gauge on the dashboard to make sure the level was correct.

Next, Avi looked at the air filter. It was grey and dusty, so he replaced it with a new one from the box he had bought at the parts shop. He also topped up the coolant reservoir, which was slightly below the minimum line.

Avi then walked around the car and pressed on each tire with his hand. The rear left tire felt soft. He took out the pump from the trunk and added air until the pressure was right. He also checked the brake pads by looking through the wheel spokes. They still had good thickness, so no change was needed.

Finally, Avi connected a tester to the battery terminals. The reading was low, which explained why the car had been slow to start lately. He decided to take it to the mechanic early in the week to get a new battery installed. He closed the hood, washed his hands, and went inside for lunch. The car was ready for another few months.
